_note: Errands: safe idle jobs you put resting pets on (the errands tab, opened by the little basket). Nobody is ever lost on an errand. Every job works the same way: a meter fills once every 'seconds' with one pet, faster with more (crew size ^ 'crew_power', so each extra pet helps a little less and spreading pets out beats stacking them), and pays 'pay' each time it's full. PAY: 'capsules' is worth that many of the capsule machine's plain capsules (Machine.coin_value), so every machine upgrade raises errands too and idle coins keep up with the machine all game (tune it well under pulling); 'coins' a fixed [min, max]; 'part' a common part each fill ('uncommon' gives a chance of an uncommon part once the crew is big enough). 'tips' multiplies a job's pay by its crew's average rarity (the lemonade stand: cute pets get bigger tips). A pet's 'stat' nudges how fast it works (rarer pets have higher stats, see Jobs.pet_speed), and 'traits' multiply it. Errands never bring rare parts or new places: those only come from adventures. Offline they run at full speed for 'offline_full_hours', then at 'offline_after' speed. 'color' is a UiTheme role, 'doodle' a UiTheme doodle. 'needs' is an unlock id (data/unlocks.json 'opens') a job waits for: until then it isn't there (the scrapyard waits for parts, a late feature; the lemonade stand opens at coin hunt lv 10). TOOLS are what coins buy on the upgrades page (the pegboard): a job's own 'tools', and the top-level 'tools' for every job. Each level costs 'capsules' (priced in the machine's plain capsules, like the pay: x Machine.coin_value, so tools keep up with the machine) x 'grow' to the power of the levels you have; 'max' 0 means no end; 'at' is the job level it waits for; 'machine' a machine tree node it waits for. 'each' is what every level does: worth (+capsules a fill), speed (fills this much sooner, added up), big (chance per fill of a big one: x 'big_x'), rare_x (tips of rare-or-better pets count this many times), all_speed (every job faster), away_hours (more hours at full speed while you're away), shiny (errand finds are shiny as often as the machine's balls, and pay like them), crew_power (each extra pet on a job helps more). A job's LEVEL is all its tools' levels added up; its 'goals' are reached at a level: 'x' multiplies its pay from then on, 'text' says what happens (an unlock with earn 'job_level' opens then); hidden until earned: a goal's 'text' only shows once it's reached, a goal with no 'x' shows no star or line ahead, and a job still to come isn't on the board at all (it just turns up at its goal). A job may have its own 'crew_power' (the savings jar: extra pets barely help). 'chunk': it pays one big lump now and then (the jar), never a stream. More PAY kinds: 'meal' feeds your active pet that much food (and 'meal_mood' mood) each fill, but only up to 'meal_upto' (the kitchen keeps it from going hungry; filling it up is still yours to do); 'note' is a scout note (see 'scout'). KITCHEN: brings nothing itself; every other job works faster by most x cooks / (cooks + half) (cooks = crew x its speed), but never more than the cooks would add on a real job with the pets on the other jobs ((1 + cooks / others) ^ crew_power - 1, so it never beats one). SCOUT: you hold up to 'hold' notes (a map case holds more; a full hold stops the meter), and a trip you send yourself to a place with something left to spot or hear takes one: 'spot' is added to each lead's spot chance, rumour chances x 'rumour_x' (never auto parties, never dungeons). 'share': false keeps share out and your pet's sharing off a job (you staff it yourself). Tool effect 'hold': more notes held. A goal can have both 'x' and 'text'. Numbers are placeholders until tools/balance.gd tunes them.
